header.name: Econometrics II
header.description:
This course will provide training in advanced applied econometrics through two (broad) modules: A) Panel Data Analysis; and B) Microeconometrics.
Panel data (or longitudinal data) run over time and for different observation units like individuals, households, firms, regions, countries, etc. The repeated nature of the individual-level data enables more realistic econometric modeling (e.g., incorporating dynamics at the individual level); more robust estimation methods (e.g., controlling for unobserved heterogeneity) and more powerful statistical inference procedures (e.g. testing for longrun purchasing power parity by pooling a number of countries). We will study the development of the linear regression model in panel data settings involving 'fixed' and 'random' effects, and the statistical propoerties of the relevant estimators. Microeconometrics is the study of economic behavior of individuals or firms by employing micro-level discrete response data and regression methods for panel data. The purpose of this module is to expose students to powerful econometric techniques frequently used in applied microeconomic research and quantitative policy analysis.
prerequisites_mandatory: ECO221Econometrics-I OR any equivalent course in statistics (Examples: Statistical Inference/Stochastic Processes and Applications/Probability and Random Processes/Statistical Signal Processing/Statistical Computation).

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Describe and apply different estimation methods for panel data, particularly addressing the unobserved individual heterogeneity in static and dynamic panel data models.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Formulate, estimate and interpret models for individuals discrete choices, and address problems with self selection and censored data.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Utilize a range of micro-econometric tools on large scale data to identify threats to uncovering causal effects from economic data and are able to interpret results.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Conduct an econometric analysis based on a real- world panel data of micro-level decision outcomes and interpret using a modern statistical software. Additionally, students will be able to critically evaluate the credibility of their model and results.

lecture_topics: Introduction to Panel Data Analysis: Advantages of Panel Data
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Four assignments; two qizzes; and a short project will be assigned based on a real-world dataset (individual or group project depending upon class-size). At the end of the semester, students will present their findings/contributions.

lecture_topics: Regression Methods for Panel Data: Fixed effects models
modeling arbitrary error structure using maximum likelihood estimation and generalized lease squares
Dynamic models with variable intercepts: MLE
Discrete Data: Some discrete response models
Dynamic discrete choice models (The general model, initial conditions, and state dependency versus heterogeneity)
Theory of probabilistic choice behavior: multiple alternative choice problems
independence of irrelevant alternatives (ordinal utilities versus scaled cardinal utilities)
Multinomial models: Additive random utility models (RUM)
Ordered, Requential and Ranked Choice Outcomes: Random parameters logit

resources.title: Analysis of Panel Data by Cheng Hsiao (Econometric Society Monographs)
Microeconometrics: Methods and Applications by A.C. Cameron and P.K. Trivedi (Cambridge University Press)
Econometric Analysis by William H. Greene (Pearson Education Inc.)
